headline: Chip rebound lifts indices, but breadth remains narrow
summary: US technology shares rebounded as semiconductors led gains, while equal-weight stocks and the Dow declined. Softer volatility and a modest credit-ETF recovery offer support, but higher Treasury yields, election uncertainty and Friday's jobs report keep the original outlook range-led.

metrics.label: Nasdaq Composite
metrics.detail: Source reports Nasdaq-100 instead: 28,180.26 (+0.68%); not interchangeable

highlights.title: Semiconductors lead a concentrated rebound
highlights.text: The semiconductor index rose 2.63%, with Nvidia up 2.29%, Broadcom 3.07% and Micron 2.58%. The equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.33% and the Dow lost 0.38%, limiting evidence of a broad recovery.

highlights.title: Credit improves modestly as yields rise
highlights.text: HYG gained 0.12% to 76.98 and VIX eased to 20.83. The Treasury 10-year par yield rose four basis points to 4.95%; the source does not count this as a confirmed directional trigger.

highlights.title: Earnings follow-through and event pricing matter
highlights.text: AMD's reported after-hours gain was provisional and is not a forecast anchor. The outlook judges its next-session close and semiconductor follow-through, while US election pricing and Friday's payrolls remain risks within the window.

forecast.outlook: Semiconductor support, narrow breadth and event uncertainty
forecast.horizon: 4–6 November US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Embedded original US outlook, section 4, using the approved newer paragraph layout; not a historical revision or the appended Australian outlook. ID is an archive locator, not an author-issued forecast ID. issued_at is the verified completed Drive modification time; precise original issue time is unavailable. Subjective probabilities, not statistically calibrated. Final-close boundaries are not technical support or resistance.
forecast.watch_next: Watch AMD's closing follow-through, semiconductor breadth, credit, election pricing and Friday's payrolls. The report's mean Brier is 0.728 across ten completed original US windows, worse than its 0.667 uniform baseline; revised forecasts are excluded.

limitations: Curated from the source report, not a new market verification. NYSE breadth, Nasdaq new lows and same-session Cboe end-of-day put/call were unavailable; non-current fund flows were not used. Nasdaq Composite was not reported; Nasdaq-100 is not substituted. The partial X handoff missed 17:00–18:00 ET. AMD after-hours and overnight futures were provisional, not forecast anchors. Oil settlement was approximate and media-reported; gold and WTI settlements were unavailable. Election counting was ongoing at the source cutoff; no outcome is asserted.
